explanation: Japan has no toilet-related taboo against the left hand like South Asia or the Middle East — being left-handed at the table isn't considered unclean or offensive. The real etiquette concerns are chopstick-specific: use whichever hand is dominant, and avoid taboos like standing chopsticks upright in rice or passing food chopstick-to-chopstick, both of which mimic funeral rites.
local_tip: If you're left-handed, it's fine to hold chopsticks in your left hand — just never stand them upright in a rice bowl or pass food directly between chopsticks, since both gestures echo funeral rituals.

also_check.note: The left hand is considered unclean from bathroom hygiene; always eat and pass food with the right hand.
Eating or passing food with the left hand is taboo; use the right hand, especially for shared dishes.
No stigma against left-hand use; left-handed diners are accommodated without issue.

sources.title: A Basic Guide to Japanese Etiquette
